- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); for first 3–5 days of a new trend, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion patterns.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates near-term (first 10 days) if sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 10% below prior 18-day average for first 5 days.
